mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Certificate of Registered Corporate Matters)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry of the District Court exercising commercial registration jurisdiction over the registered office, Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Korean domestic document: no apostille or legalization is required for domestic Korean use. If it must be used outside Korea, obtain an apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs only if the destination is an Apostille Convention member; for non-member destinations obtain consular legalization. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent extract of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registrar or company registry in the jurisdiction of each foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Foreign-origin document: if the issuing jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention member, notarize and affix an apostille issued by the local competent authority; if the issuing jurisdiction is not an Apostille Convention member, notarize, authenticate through the issuing state's foreign ministry, then legalize at the Consular Section of the Embassy of the Republic of Korea in that state. These paths are parallel alternatives; no sequential combination is allowed.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution and power of attorney authorizing the incorporation representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the foreign corporate shareholder or the sole founder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Foreign-origin document: notarize in the country of origin; if an Apostille Convention member, issue a local apostille; if a non-member, obtain prescribed local authentication and then consular legalization from the Republic of Korea Embassy/Consulate. Use only one authentication path, never both.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public, Republic of Korea, in coordination with the incorporation representatives
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Korean domestic instrument: notarized under Korean notarial law. No foreign apostille/legalization is required for Korean registration. Subsequent foreign use would follow the MOFA apostille path or consular legalization path depending exclusively on destination membership.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter for the founder or foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank in the jurisdiction where the founder maintains its primary relationship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the bank is in an Apostille Convention state, the signed letter must be notarized and apostilled by the state's competent authority. If the bank is in a non-member state, the letter must be notarized, authenticated by the local ministry of foreign affairs, and then consular legalized at the Republic of Korea's diplomatic mission. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive alternatives.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO declaration and disclosure schedule completed by each ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ultimate beneficial owners and directors, acknowledged before a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic Korean notarization applies for Korean signatories. For any foreign signatory, the signed declaration must be notarized in the country of signature and then either apostilled (apostille member) or consular legalized (non-member). Do not combine the two modes.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every UBO, director, officer, authorized signatory, and beneficial owner must be screened before incorporation and on an ongoing basis against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the OFAC SDN and non-SDN sanctions lists, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the Korean Government's financial sanctions designations, and the KoFIU/FSC AML list. Foreign PEPs, their immediate family members, and close associates require enhanced due diligence under the Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Transaction Information. For USDC and cryptocurrency settlement rails, blockchain wallet screening against OFAC- and UN-sanctioned addresses and travel-rule compliant counterparty identification is mandatory before onboarding any corporate customer.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Commercial Registration Information System (CRIS) and Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (i-ROS) at www.iros.go.kr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A Korean company name must be filed in Hangul script. The name of a limited liability company must end with the legal form suffix Yuhan Hoesa; the standard four-tier structure is primary distinctive name, business objective, legal form suffix, and registered office district. An English or other foreign-language trade name may be registered as an additional trade name only when a Hangul transliteration and English transcription are supplied and the name does not mislead the public. Prohibited characters, non-verbal symbols, and confusingly similar existing names are rejected.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registry officer refuses a name clearance or incorporation application, the applicant may file a written objection with the registry office and an appeal for adjudication to the district court with jurisdiction under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act within 14 days of notice. The appeal must identify the specific refusal, attach corrected Articles of Association, and state why the proposed name is distinguishable and not misleading. The court may reverse or affirm. If affirmative, the applicant must refile under a fresh name. A name reservation is not renewable; a new application is required after the 30-day validity window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office or commercial mailbox without a physical lease, physical staff, and equipment is generally rejected by the National Tax Service for business registration and by Korean banks for corporate account opening under the Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality Act. For an AI/LLM API platform accepting Stripe and USDC, a serviced office with a dedicated physical suite, a lease agreement, on-site reception, and visible engineering/operations capability is the minimum credible substance. A mailbox-only address will trigger adverse tax conforming audits and account restriction.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced on-site inspection risk is moderate at 30-45% in the first two years because the business model includes high-volume digital API sales and cryptocurrency settlement rails. Inspection checklist: current lease matching the registered address; on-site management or employees; utility and telecommunications invoices in the company name; functioning servers, terminals, and engineering records; books, VAT invoices, and bank statements at the address; Stripe and USDC settlement records; authorized representative's identity documents; and a Korean-language business name plaque at the entrance.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial registration court fee and education surtax for a limited liability company with estimated paid-in capital of KRW 100 million
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: District Court Registry / Supreme Court of Korea
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Commercial Registration Fee Schedule: registration fee equals 0.4% of capital, plus 20% education surtax; estimated market cost.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Business registration certificate and tax office certificate of business commencement
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: National Tax Service / local tax office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official administrative fee for business registration certificate; nominal amount.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of Articles of Association, board resolutions, and UBO declarations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Korean Notary Fee Act and prevailing notarial tariff based on document complexity; estimated for five instruments.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: External legal counsel: pre-incorporation due diligence, name search, UBO piercing, AML policy drafting, and filing support
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing Korean cross-border corporate and AML market rate for a low-risk technology LLC; blended fixed/time basis.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization fees for foreign-issued corporate and banking documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent foreign apostille authorities and Consular Section of the Republic of Korea Embassies/Consulates
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official legalization fees range from USD 50-150 per document plus apostille fees; estimated USD 150 average for five documents.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered address / serviced office in Seoul for 12 months
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Seoul serviced-office market benchmark of approximately USD 150 per month for a qualifying physical suite.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Annual subscription benchmark for a small commercial entity conducting daily OFAC/UN/Korea list screening and PEP checks.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Act No. 1000 as amended, Articles 288 through 313; particularly Article 290 on contents of Articles of Incorporation, Article 292 on registration of incorporation, Article 312 on directors and auditor for a Yuhan Hoesa, and Article 313 on the incorporation registration application; implemented under the Registration Tax Act and the Notary Public Act of Korea.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registry Office of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office of the company, operated through the Supreme Court of the Republic of Korea Internet Registration Office (I-REG).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Corporate Incorporation Registration Application, submitted with notarized Articles of Incorporation, bank capital deposit certificate, registered-office lease consent, statutory officer acceptance forms, and corporate seal registration documents.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under the Korean Commercial Act; however, the full issued share capital stated in the Articles of Incorporation must be deposited into a blocked bank escrow account in Korea before the registration application is filed, and the bank-issued capital payment certificate must accompany the filing; the escrow restriction is released only after the corporate registration is completed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF YUHAN HOESA. WHEREAS, Yuhan Hoesa is a limited liability company being organized under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea; WHEREAS, the Company's Articles of Incorporation were duly executed and notarized by the initial shareholders and promoters; WHEREAS, the Company's registered capital has been fully subscribed and is set out in the incorporation registration application; WHEREAS, the Commercial Act and the registry practice require the Company to establish its corporate bank account, adopt its registered office, and appoint its statutory officers before or immediately after the incorporation registration filing; and WHEREAS, all actions authorized in this resolution are lawful, within the objects of the Company, and in the best interests of the Company and its shareholders. NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS. 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: The paid-in share capital of the Company as recorded in the capital subscription table and in the registration application, together with any share premium, is hereby approved, ratified, and declared fully subscribed and paid in cash by the persons named in the subscription schedule. The Chief Executive Officer, acting with the incorporators where necessary, is authorized to verify the bank capital payment confirmation issued by the depositary bank of the escrow account and to file that confirmation with the competent Registry as the statutory proof of capital payment. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: The Company shall open and maintain corporate bank accounts, including a KRW operating account, a multi-currency account, and settlement-facilitator accounts required for Stripe, USDC, and other payment rails, with one or more licensed banks selected by the Chief Executive Officer. The Chief Executive Officer, or any director designated by the Chief Executive Officer, is hereby authorized to execute all account opening forms, signature cards, online banking mandates, currency control declarations, and banking agreements. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: The location described as the Company's registered office in the Articles of Incorporation and in the incorporation registration application is hereby adopted as the Company's statutory address for notices, process service, tax registration, and regulatory communications. The Chief Executive Officer is authorized to execute and ratify the lease, service, and office-management agreements necessary for that address and to appoint any registered-office service agent. 4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS: The chief executive officer named in the incorporation documents is appointed as Chief Executive Officer of the Company. The auditor named in the incorporation documents, or otherwise required under Article 312 of the Commercial Act, is appointed as statutory auditor; if the Company qualifies for the statutory auditor exemption, the Board confirms that exemption as permitted by law. The Chief Executive Officer is granted full authority to represent the Company in all commercial and regulatory affairs, to sign contracts, to hire employees, to operate payment systems, and to make routine tax filings. The auditor, if appointed, shall have the powers and duties provided by the Commercial Act. 5. AUTHORIZATION AND RATIFICATION: Any lawful act performed by any incorporator, officer, or attorney before the date of this resolution for the purpose of organizing the Company, reserving the name, opening depositary accounts, obtaining the office lease, engaging consultants, or preparing the registration filing is hereby ratified and confirmed. 6. EFFECTIVENESS: This resolution is effective immediately and may be executed in counterparts. The Company Secretary or Chief Executive Officer is directed to provide certified copies of this resolution to the Registry, banks, tax authorities, and other third parties as reasonably required. ADOPTED UNANIMOUSLY by the Board and incorporators on the date first written above.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation corporate name clearance and notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court of the Republic of Korea Internet Registration Office (I-REG) and a licensed Korean notary public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform a preliminary name search in the I-REG database to confirm that the proposed corporate name is not identical or confusingly similar to any registered company. After name clearance, prepare the Articles of Incorporation specifying the corporate purpose of generative AI software development, large language model hosting, AI inference API services, and related information technology consulting. Submit the draft to a licensed Korean notary, who will verify the identity and capacity of the incorporators. Notarization must be completed before the registration application is accepted. For non-resident incorporators, deliver notarized passport copies and apostilled powers of attorney if the incorporator is represented by an agent.
required_dossiers: Corporate name reservation or name search output
Passport or national identity documents of all incorporators
Apostilled or consularized power of attorney, if applicable
Proof of incorporator address and foreign tax identification numbers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name search returns a conflict or similarity objection, select a secondary corporate name and submit a new reservation. If the notary raises a formal defect in the Articles, amend the Articles and re-notarize before proceeding to the next step.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of restricted capital escrow deposit account and issuance of bank capital payment certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any licensed commercial bank in the Republic of Korea authorized to issue capital payment verification certificates for corporate incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary company-in-formation escrow account in the name of the promoter or the company being formed. The bank will place a restricted-withdrawal condition on the account until the court Registry confirms incorporation. Deposit the full issued share capital stated in the Articles into the account and request the bank's capital payment certificate, which must show the depositor name, account number, balance, and deposit date. The certificate should be dated no earlier than ten calendar days before the filing date. If capital is paid in foreign currency, the bank must issue a conversion confirmation in KRW. This certificate is the mandatory evidence of paid-in capital for the incorporation registration.
required_dossiers: Identification documents of all incorporators and beneficial owners
Anti-money laundering customer due diligence forms
Source-of-funds documentation where deposit amount exceeds internal bank thresholds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional anti-money laundering clarification, submit bank statements, transaction records, or source-of-wealth evidence. If the bank refuses to lift account restrictions or cannot issue the certificate, close the account and reopen with another licensed bank without changing the capital amount.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of the incorporation registration application to the competent District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registry Office of the District Court with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office, using the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office (I-REG) portal or in-person filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Corporate Incorporation Registration Application with the Registry together with the notarized Articles, the bank capital payment certificate, the lease contract for the registered office with the landlord’s written consent, the written acceptance of appointment of each statutory officer, and the corporate seal application if a seal will be used. Pay the registration tax, local education tax, and court filing fee. The registration officer will examine the documents for compliance with the Commercial Act and the Registration Tax Act. Upon approval, the company is entered into the commercial register, the corporate identification number is issued, and the company becomes a legal entity. Foreign shareholders should verify whether any Foreign Investment Promotion Act filing threshold applies.
required_dossiers: Registered-office lease agreement and landlord consent
Written acceptance of appointment by statutory officers
Identification documents of directors, CEO, auditor, and shareholders
Corporate seal imprint specimen and seal registration request
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a correction or supplemental documents order, respond within the statutory correction period by filing the requested clarifications. If the application is finally rejected, file a new application with corrected documents and pay the relevant fees again.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business registration with the National Tax Service for corporate income tax, VAT, and e-invoicing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Tax Office of the National Tax Service (NTS) with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within the statutory period after incorporation, submit the corporate business registration application to the competent District Tax Office. Attach the certified corporate register certificate, the Articles of Incorporation, the corporate seal certificate, the registered-office lease, the CEO identification, and the completed business registration form. The NTS will assign the corporate business registration number, register the company for corporate income tax, register the company for value-added tax, and enable the electronic tax invoice system. The company must update its business scope code to reflect computer programming and AI platform services. The bank account activation and customer contracting are typically blocked until the business registration certificate is issued.
required_dossiers: Identification of the Chief Executive Officer
Bank account details and incorporation registration number
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NTS queries the application because the address or business code is inconsistent, correct the registry record and lease details and resubmit. If the tax office assigns an incorrect business code, submit an amended business registration application and request reclassification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory social insurance enrollment and operating bank account activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korea Social Security Information Service through the Four Major Social Insurances integrated reporting system and the designated Korean commercial bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as a workplace with the national pension, national health insurance, employment insurance, and industrial accident compensation insurance schemes through the integrated social insurance reporting system. Submit the business registration certificate, corporate register certificate, CEO identification, and employee list. After completion, activate the company’s operating bank accounts by presenting the corporate register certificate, NTS business registration certificate, corporate seal certificate, an excerpt of the First Board Resolution, and the authorized signatories’ identification. For the AI and LLM API platform, complete the bank’s AML and beneficial ownership declaration and, if required, the risk assessment for accepting Stripe or USDC settlement flows.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution excerpt for banking authorization
Employee list and employment start dates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the social insurance portal rejects the registration because of data mismatches, reconcile the corporate register and employee records before resubmission. If the bank delays account activation, provide the missing seal certificates or board excerpts under the same resolution and escalate to the branch compliance officer.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate seal registration, share certificate issuance, and statutory books preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registry Office of the District Court for corporate seal certificate; company management for share certificates and statutory records
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, register the corporate seal imprint with the Registry and obtain the corporate seal certificate, which is the standard executing instrument for contracts, tax filings, bank forms, and payment facility agreements. Issue physical share certificates to all shareholders and record the allotment in the shareholder register and share certificate stubs. Maintain the corporate minutes book, statutory ledger, and the First Board Resolution at the registered office. If the company will accept USDC, document clearly that the company is a merchant using third-party payment gateways and not a virtual asset service provider requiring separate licensing under Korean financial law. Confirm whether an external audit exemption applies based on the company’s asset size after the first year.
required_dossiers: Identification of the CEO and shareholders
Board resolution authorizing issuance of share certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry delays the seal certificate due to an unresolved incorporation condition, first cure that condition at the Registry and reapply. If a share certificate is spoilt or lost, cancel it by board minute and reissue under the corporate seal with an indemnity letter.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - ISIC 6201 (computer programming, AI and LLM API platform) is a pure digital and consulting activity with no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing establishment requiring industrial licensing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no factory or plant operating license is required. The company must only maintain ordinary commercial registration, comply with the Korean data protection framework, and, where applicable, file any value-added telecommunications service report with the Ministry of Science and ICT if its online service meets the threshold; this is not an industrial operating permit.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - the Ministry of Environment and its Korea Environment Corporation have no permitting jurisdiction over an office-based software and API platform activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - the business is not listed in the schedules of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act and does not trigger an environmental registration category because there is no physical production facility, no land disturbance, and no hazardous waste generation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - zero wastewater discharge, zero VOC emissions, and zero hazardous waste handling. Any ordinary office waste must be removed by a licensed municipal or private waste collector, and any end-of-life IT equipment shall be recycled through the approved electronic waste channel.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for industrial Civil Defense permitting. The company’s ordinary office must, however, comply with the Building Fire Protection and Evacuation Act by maintaining fire extinguishers, evacuation routes, emergency lighting, and a current fire safety inspection certificate from the district fire department; the operation does not cross the threshold for a separate industrial civil defense license.

stage_2.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for industrial Civil Defense permitting. The company’s ordinary office must, however, comply with the Building Fire Protection and Evacuation Act by maintaining fire extinguishers, evacuation routes, emergency lighting, and a current fire safety inspection certificate from the district fire department; the operation does not cross the threshold for a separate industrial civil defense license.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online electronic portal: Home Tax Service (hometax.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-invested Korean Yuhan Hoesa, the statutory Taxpayer Identification Number is the 10-digit Business Registration Number issued under the Value-Added Tax Act and the Framework Act on National Taxes. The foreign non-resident shareholder must first complete the Korean corporate registration at the local court registry office, and where applicable file a foreign investment report with a Korean foreign exchange bank or Invest Korea. After incorporation, the company must submit a Business Registration Application to the district tax office that has jurisdiction over the principal place of business, or use the NTS Home Tax Service online registration channel. Supporting documents include the certificate of corporate registration, articles of incorporation, tenant contract or ownership proof of the registered office, identity documents and power of attorney of the representative director, and, for a foreign-owned company, copies of the shareholder's identity documents and foreign entity formation certificates. For a branch of a foreign company, the parent company's certificate of incorporation, evidence of corporate existence from the home-country registrar, and the Korean branch registration certificate are also required. The NTS issues a 10-digit Business Registration Number that functions as the VAT identification number, corporate tax identifier, and employer withholding account number. If the entity will export physical goods, it must also obtain an exporter code from the Korea Customs Service through the UNI-PASS electronic customs clearance portal; for pure digital AI API exports, no separate customs exporter registration is required, but the NTS registration remains mandatory before taxable supplies commence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Republic of Korea does not allow a check-the-box or pass-through election for a Yuhan Hoesa. The company is taxed at the entity level under the Corporate Tax Act; no statutory hybrid-mismatch or check-the-box election is available for treatment as a disregarded entity.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No statutory turnover threshold. Any business supplying taxable goods or services in Korea is required to register for VAT upon commencement of taxable activity; a foreign non-resident supplier of digital services to Korean consumers may also have separate simplified registration obligations under the Korean VAT digital services rules, but for a resident Korean entity registration is mandatory from the first taxable supply with no KRW threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT-registered taxpayers of general-taxpayer status must issue electronic tax invoices through the NTS-governed Home Tax System e-invoice service or through a certified ERP/accounting system connected to the NTS e-invoice interface. Electronic tax invoice data is transmitted to the NTS on or before the statutory VAT tax invoice issuance deadline, generally the 10th day of the month following the date of supply, and the NTS stores and validates the data against business registration records, sequential invoice numbers, and transaction counterparties. South Korea does not operate a pre-clearance digital stamping or fiscal seal system; anti-fraud enforcement uses centralized NTS e-invoice database matching, mandatory electronic transmission of tax invoice data, automatic denial of input VAT deduction where the e-tax invoice is not properly transmitted, mandatory cash-receipt devices for certain B2C businesses, and cross-matching of VAT returns with corporate tax, customs and foreign-exchange data.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act, export of goods is zero-rated when the goods are actually exported from the Republic of Korea under a Korea Customs Service export declaration. Services are zero-rated where they constitute foreign exchange earning services under the Enforcement Decree of the Value-Added Tax Act: the service is supplied to a nonresident or a foreign enterprise, the service is actually used or enjoyed outside Korea, and the consideration is received in foreign currency or in Korean won under lawful foreign-exchange settlement. For an AI/LLM API platform, qualifying zero-rating requires a written service contract with a nonresident customer, evidence that the API consumer and inference processing are supplied for use outside Korea, nonresident customer verification through foreign tax registration, incorporation documents, habitual residence, foreign IP address or foreign payment method, and actual inbound remittance from the overseas customer. A zero-rated export invoice must be reported in the VAT return; input VAT attributable to the zero-rated export may be recovered through the standard NTS VAT refund procedure.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service electronic Export Declaration (UNI-PASS clearance receipt for goods)
Commercial invoice and detailed export description of the goods or services
Bill of Lading, air waybill, or transport documentation proving actual removal of goods from Korea
For digital services: signed end-user service agreement, API usage and delivery logs, and nonresident customer tax-residence evidence
Foreign exchange inward remittance certificate or receipt issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank evidencing receipt of export proceeds from the foreign customer
Foreign exchange settlement confirmation or extended settlement approval as required under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS cross-checks export zero-rating claims against Korea Customs Service export clearance records, foreign exchange bank reports, electronic tax invoices, service usage logs, and nonresident identification data. If a zero-rating claim is rejected because the required documentation bundle is incomplete, the export proceeds are not repatriated within 180 days without an approved foreign-exchange extension, the nonresident recipient is not substantiated, or the service is determined to be consumed in Korea, the NTS will retrospectively assess output VAT at the standard 10% rate on the full supply value, plus penalty surcharges, false-tax-invoice penalties where applicable, and statutory late-payment interest running from the original VAT return due date. A fraudulent claim involving a false tax invoice, false export declaration, or intentionally fabricated export documentation is subject to criminal sanctions under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act and the Value-Added Tax Act, including imprisonment, fines, and extended assessment periods of up to 10 years for intentional tax evasion or false export claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) as the paramount monetary and central banking authority, jointly administered with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; the Korea Customs Service also supervises physical cross-border currency movements, and the Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) enforces AML/CFT supervision over designated foreign exchange banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Korean won is classified as a freely usable currency for current-account transactions under a notification-based system rather than an approval-licensing system for routine trade and service payments. Inward capital injections such as equity contributions to a domestic LLC must be declared through a designated foreign exchange bank using the capital transaction reporting module; after declaration, funds are credited to an escrow/settlement account and can be converted at the onshore won-dollar market rate. Outbound profit remittances are permitted once the entity proves the source of the dividend, pays the applicable 15.4% corporate withholding tax or secures a tax treaty certificate, and files a payment report with the bank. Korea does not maintain a cycling surrender system for export receipts, but all export proceeds must be repatriated and collected within the statutory period, and receipts below certain thresholds may be covered by simplified procedures. The actual convertibility bottleneck is not legal but documentary: exchange banks require source-of-funds evidence, UBO clarity, tax completion certificates, and proper BOK reporting before processing dividends, loan repayments, capital repatriation, or large intercompany transfers. Non-resident shareholders cannot simply wire funds; they need disclosure forms, beneficial-owner declarations, proof of lawful foreign exchange, and alignment with the declared business purpose of the LLC.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its Enforcement Decree, export proceeds must be collected within 6 months from the contract date or shipping date, extendable up to 18 months for legitimate trade credit terms after approval by a designated foreign exchange bank. There is no blanket mandatory conversion of export receipts into KRW at a fixed surrendered ratio; the operational requirement is that all export receipts must be routed through a designated foreign exchange bank in Korea, reported into the Foreign Exchange Information System, and, only when conversion to KRW is required for domestic payments, sold at the onshore market exchange rate.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital escrow and operational KRW settlement account plus foreign-currency current account for LLC funding
Capital investment escrow account and multi-currency operational account with trade finance capabilities
Capital verification account for equity injection and regular treasury settlement account
Corporate KRW operating account with designated foreign exchange bank status and capital transaction reporting module

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a standalone primary banking relationship. Foreign fintech EMIs are not licensed by Korea to open KRW settlement accounts, issue corporate accounts, or provide formal foreign exchange declaration services under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. A digital EMI may act only as a supplementary collection conduit if it partners with a licensed Korean designated foreign exchange bank, but the legal treasury rail and capital verification must remain with a domestic bank. Korean internet-only banks such as KakaoBank and Toss Bank are domestic banks, yet their corporate onboarding remains limited for the scale and cross-border AI API business of this entity; therefore, they are unsuitable as the primary treasury counterparty.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-branch physical appearance by at least one statutory representative or a formally appointed senior officer with power of attorney is the expected baseline for the initial corporate KYC interview. Remote consular proxy account opening is occasionally accepted if the proxy holds a notarized and apostilled power of attorney endorsed by the Korean consulate, but most designated foreign exchange banks will still require a recorded video interview and a physical branch visit before activating cross-border capital transactions. For a non-resident director, a valid passport, alien registration card where applicable, corporate registration extract, and seal certificate or equivalent execution proof must be presented.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border capital injection from a non-resident shareholder into the LLC for a token-based AI API platform with no clear offline operational footprint
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified board resolution in Korean, capital remittance instruction, source-of-funds statement, 12-month bank statements of the transferring entity, subscription price calculation, AML questionnaire for all directors, apostilled and notarized corporate documents, shareholder register up to ultimate natural persons, and a signed explanation of the AI API contracts, customer pipeline, and revenue model that validates commercial purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of Cryptocurrency or USDC as a target payment rail, creating virtual asset exposure and requiring enhanced AML scrutiny
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A compliance certificate showing conformity with the Korean Virtual Asset User Protection Act, proof that any USDC settlement is cleared only through a licensed Korean virtual asset exchange, robust travel-rule transaction monitoring, wallet screening, sanctions and adverse-media checks, hot and cold wallet controls, transaction suspicious activity policies, and a legal memorandum from a Korean counsel confirming the exchange of virtual assets into KRW will be reported to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Nominee or representative-director structure with insufficient economic substance and a discrepancy between the declared domicile and actual management location
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete beneficial ownership register leading to natural persons, employment agreements, lease or local office contracts demonstrating Korea substance, local tax and social insurance filings, board minutes proving strategic and operating decision-making, and a translated KYC interview transcript documenting the director's understanding of the LLC's cross-border treasury and payment flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency cross-border service payments for AI API fees with potential mis-declared purpose code and unreported settlement data
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transaction-level ledger of API calls and downstream clients, executed contracts and invoices, corresponding SWIFT MT103 payment records, a detailed purpose-code mapping under the Korean Foreign Exchange Information System aligned with ISIC 6201, and an independent sector narrative showing the company generates core income from generative AI inference and LLM API tokens rather than dormant holding activity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The LLC must open a capital escrow KRW account with a designated foreign exchange bank before receiving any equity funding. The non-resident shareholder should file a capital transaction declaration through that designated bank, using the Foreign Exchange Information System purpose code for inbound foreign direct investment and equity participation. The actual wire must arrive via SWIFT MT103 with the beneficiary bank, LLC name, and a clear remittance reference matching the declaration; upon receipt, the designated bank shall verify the foreign currency amount, issue a certificate of receipt of foreign capital or capital verification confirmation, convert the funds to KRW at the market rate, and deposit them into the escrow capital account. For subsequent injections, each transfer must be covered by a fresh declaration or amendments, and the cumulative capital register must trace every contribution to the official share allocation records.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlements and operational disbursements, the primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 through the designated Korean bank, with cross-border KRW or USD payments processed over the global SWIFT infrastructure. Commercial letters of credit and documentary collections are only appropriate when the counterparty transacts in physical goods or requires a transmissive finance instrument; for AI API licensing and SaaS services, clean MT103 telegraphic transfers under the correct service-import purpose code are faster and more compliant. Domestic disbursements should be executed through Korea's BOK-Wire plus system, while payments to Stripe or other payment facilitators must be structured as settlement transfers to a licensed acquiring bank, not as hidden overseas banking transactions. USDC and other virtual asset outflows are permissible only when routed through a properly licensed Korean virtual asset exchange and must remain distinct from bank clearing rails.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore forward foreign exchange contracts for documented current-account and trade-related exposures between the LLC and its designated bank
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts for non-resident counterparties hedging KRW exposure when no deliverable onshore KRW account exists
Currency swaps and long-term foreign-exchange swaps permitted for non-speculative balance-sheet hedging of foreign currency debt or intercompany liabilities
Plain-vanilla KRW/USD options where the premium and settlement remain fully compliant with the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the bank's KYC documentation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Regular General Meeting of Members (Annual Members' Assembly) — convene and record corporate acts and financial approvals
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company corporate records (minutes retained at registered office; if shareholders' meeting minutes are notarized, the notary is the custodian)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three (3) calendar months after the end of each fiscal year (i.e., by March 31 for a December 31 year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the annual meeting is a criminal summary offense under the Commercial Act exposing responsible managers to a fine up to KRW 5 million (approx. USD 3,800); no direct deregistration, but repeated non-convening can draw a court order for judicial inspection and ultimately dissolute winding-up.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return and Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via the HomeTax system (South Korea)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three (3) months after fiscal year end (by March 31 for calendar-year firms); a one-month extension may be granted upon application
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a 20% negligence penalty on unpaid tax plus 0.022% per day (8% pa) late-payment interest; late filing beyond the extended deadline is treated as non-filing, allowing NTS to make a mandatory assessment. Persistent non-filing for two or more years can result in cancellation of the business registration certificate, tax seizure of assets, and potential delisting of the entity from the commercial registry as a dormant company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Local Income Tax Return and Payment (Local Corporate Surtax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government of the registered office (competent metropolitan city/province taxation authority; integrated filing via NTS HomeTax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as corporate income tax return: within three (3) months after fiscal year end (by March 31 for calendar-year companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Local tax delinquency attracts the same 20% negligence penalty on the local income tax and 0.022% per day late-payment interest; arbitrary reassessment can be issued by the municipal tax collector if the return is not submitted, with eventual forced collection against bank accounts and real estate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Annual Business Report (if the company qualifies as a foreign-invested enterprise)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) or a designated foreign exchange bank (submission through the InvestKorea system or the applicable bank)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after fiscal year end (by March 31 for calendar-year companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing of the annual business report may lead to a fine of up to KRW 10 million (approx. USD 7,600) under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, and loss of foreign-investment incentives (tax credits, foreign exchange protections) for the investors.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Certified Auditor's Report (only if the company meets the statutory thresholds under the External Audit Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) and, if applicable, the Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) (external audit report repository)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be completed and submitted together with the annual corporate tax return (by March 31 for calendar-year firms) or before the shareholders' meeting if the articles require earlier
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to obtain a statutory audit when mandated is an offense under the External Audit Act punishable by a fine up to KRW 50 million (approx. USD 38,000) for the company and imprisonment / fines for the managing compliance officers; unqualified opinion may trigger a separate review by the FSS and formal sanctions against directors.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Korean External Audit Act (Act on External Audit of Joint-stock Companies, etc.) and its Enforcement Decree, a Yuhan Hoesa must appoint an independent certified CPA auditor if, as of the end of the preceding fiscal year, its total assets reach or exceed KRW 12 billion (approx. USD 9 million); or if total assets reach or exceed KRW 7 billion (approx. USD 5.3 million) and the company has (i) an average of 100 or more employees, (ii) 500 or more members/shareholders, or (iii) paid-in capital of KRW 3 billion or more. Korean law does not impose a standalone turnover (revenue) threshold; however, the Financial Supervisory Service may, on a case-by-case basis, designate a company to submit to an external audit if the annual turnover exceeds a level indicating the need for investor protection.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Non-listed entities subject to audit typically apply Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) or Korean GAAP (the General Corporate Accounting Standards). Small and medium enterprises not subject to audit may use the Korean SME Accounting Standards. The audit must be performed in accordance with the Korean Standards on Auditing (KSA).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korean law does not impose a standalone annual UBO confirmation return on a Yuhan Hoesa. However, the Foreign Investment Promotion Act requires foreign-invested companies to report any change in shareholding or ultimate beneficial ownership to MOTIE or a designated bank within 30 days of the change. Moreover, the company must maintain an up-to-date register of members reflecting all transfers of membership interests; every transfer must be recorded in the register on the date of effect, and a transfer is only valid upon entry. There is no 12-month anniversary UBO filing with a court register.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Register of Charges/Mortgages, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 – USD 2,500 per year (typical outsourced registered office and compliance agent services in Seoul/Incheon)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 – USD 25,000 per year (for a small/medium technology company subject to a mandatory audit or engaging a voluntary review; large audits may exceed USD 50,000)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.4% aggregate headline (24% national corporate income tax plus 2.4% local income-tax surtax) on income above KRW 300 billion; lower brackets at 9.9%, 20.9%, and 23.1%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Free Economic Zone foreign-invested AI/advanced IT services may qualify for a 50% corporate income tax reduction for the first 3 years and an additional 2-year 50% reduction under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act; qualifying AI/LLM R&D expenditures may earn tax credits up to 30%; SME preferential rates and R&D facility investment credits also apply.
